title.value: Technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings: A scoping review and feasibility analysis of educational technologies
title.justification: The title provides a concise summary of the paper's focus on technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings, specifically examining the feasibility of different educational technologies for low- and middle-income countries.
title.quote: Technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings: A scoping review and feasibility analysis of educational technologies

extractions.description: This paper investigates the use of educational technologies to improve trauma training in low- and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs). It conducts a scoping review of existing technologies used in trauma courses and evaluates their feasibility for use in LMICs. The study found that high-fidelity mannequins, though effective, were not suitable due to high costs and maintenance challenges, while virtual simulation and digital courses showed higher feasibility scores for these settings.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on enhancing trauma training in low- and lower-middle-income countries, addressing the need for educational technologies that are feasible and effective in these low-resource settings.
primary_category.quote: ...this is the first study to perform a feasibility analysis of trauma training technologies in the LMIC context. We identified that the majority of trauma courses in the literature use technologies which are less suitable for LMICs.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper primarily focuses on educational technologies in the context of healthcare and does not explicitly relate to other eco-responsible AI categories outside of its application to the Global South.
secondary_categories.quote: Given the urgent need for pediatric trauma training, educators must use technologies that optimize learning outcomes and remain feasible for low-resource settings.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper shares insights and analyses regarding technology-enhanced trauma training that may inform policy and practice in LMICs, particularly suited for low-resource environments.
primary_sub_category.quote: ...educators must use technologies that optimize learning outcomes and remain feasible for low-resource settings.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The focus is specifically on trauma training technologies and their feasibility in LMICs, without branching into other sub-categories beyond policy and knowledge sharing.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Despite their effectiveness, high-fidelity mannequins ranked poorly in production, maintenance, cost, and reusability categories, therefore being poorly suited for LMICs.

applications.value: Feasibility evaluation of educational technologies for trauma training in LMICs
applications.justification: The paper evaluates various educational technologies for their feasibility in trauma training within low-resource settings, providing valuable insights into their applicability and effectiveness in LMICs.
applications.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first study to perform a feasibility analysis of trauma training technologies in the LMIC context.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper fits within existing categories, primarily addressing support to the Global South through technology-enhanced learning for trauma training.
new_primary_category.quote: We conducted a scoping review evaluating the learning outcomes of technology-enhanced training in general trauma assessment...

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The focus on policy advice and knowledge sharing in the context of education technology for LMICs fits within existing sub-categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Based on the Technology-Enhanced Learning criteria, we created and applied a feasibility analysis tool to evaluate the technologies for use in LMICs.
